**Technically yes, but your own rules file says no**: it lists `is.waiwai.dictation` as permanent because existing Accessibility permission grants depend on it. You can override that as the owner, and pre-launch is the cheapest time you will ever have to do it.

macOS keys privacy permissions to the bundle identifier, so a rename makes the app look like a brand-new app. For anyone who already has a build installed, that means:

- **Accessibility grant is lost.** They must re-approve in System Settings, and the old entry stays behind as a stale row. For a dictation app, text insertion fails until they do.
- **Microphone and any other privacy grants reset** the same way.
- **Preferences reset**, because `UserDefaults` is stored under the bundle ID. The same goes for any Application Support or Caches paths and Keychain items derived from it.
- **Login item registration** may need to be redone.
- **Sparkle updates across the rename need testing.** The EdDSA key stays the same, but I would test an old-ID to new-ID update end to end before relying on it.

The decision turns on who has the app installed today:

- **Only you and a few testers:** rename now. Everyone re-grants once, and the name matches the product from launch onward.
- **A real user base (public beta, earlier releases):** I would keep the identifier. Users never see it, and the cost is silent breakage for every one of them.

Renaming after launch should be off the table either way.

If you go ahead, update the invariant in the rules file to the new identifier in the same change. I can't see the repository in this session, so I can't tell you how many places reference the ID (Info.plist, entitlements, the Sparkle appcast, `docs/release.md`, `AGENTS.md`, signing and notarization scripts); that needs a repo-wide search for `is.waiwai.dictation`.

Who has builds installed right now?
